headline: A rough night on Wall Street dragged into Sunday's ASX session — PLS and GXAI led the local losses while the NASDAQ shed over 4% last night.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: PLS had a tough session today, dropping 3.75% to $5.91. Lithium sentiment globally is getting crushed — a Reuters/NAI500 report flagged that top Chinese lithium miners are crashing, dragging the whole sector lower. There's no near-term floor in sight while Chinese supply keeps overwhelming demand.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft fell 2.66% last night in a broad tech selloff that hammered the NASDAQ (down 4.18%). No specific Microsoft news drove it — this was the whole market repricing risk, likely tied to concerns around Trump's new AI regulation order which could add compliance hurdles for big tech.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: GXAI dropped 1.74% today, reflecting the sharp NASDAQ selloff from last night. This ETF tracks global AI companies, so when US tech gets hammered (NASDAQ -4.18% last night), GXAI follows. Ironically, multiple analysts still named it as a top pick for the 'AI decade' this week.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Take-Two slipped 1.04% last night as part of the broader NASDAQ selloff. No company-specific bad news — GTA V was in the headlines for being a still-dominant open-world game, which is a positive backdrop, but the macro selloff overwhelmed it.

movers.name: Alphabet (Google)
movers.note: Google fell 0.95% last night in a tough session for the whole NASDAQ. Trump's new AI regulation executive order — which would give the government more oversight over how companies like Google launch AI models — may be adding an overhang on Alphabet's AI growth story.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE edged down 0.94% today. Emerging markets tracked lower as the Aussie dollar weakened (AUD/USD dropped 1.16% last night), which adds currency headwinds for this ETF. China-linked sentiment also softened on the lithium/commodity news.

movers.name: BetaShares Global Energy ETF
movers.note: FUEL slipped 0.8% today after Goldman Sachs cut their oil demand forecast, warning of 'big hit' to global consumption and flagging downside risks to prices. Crude oil fell 2.69% last night to $90.54/barrel, which weighed on energy company share prices worldwide.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG barely budged today, up just 0.12% to $75.95. Its diversified mix across asset classes acted as a buffer — while the US tech-heavy portion dragged, the broader diversification kept it roughly flat. Steady as she goes.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: VTS managed a small gain of 0.31% today despite last night's NASDAQ carnage. This is likely a timing lag — ASX-listed ETFs that track the US market can trade with a delay to the actual US session. Expect some catch-up pressure when US markets open tonight.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX — Lithium rout deepening
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals dropped another 3.75% today to $5.91, and is now down 12.3% on your cost base. Chinese lithium miners are crashing on oversupply fears and Goldman Sachs is cutting commodity demand forecasts. Until there's a clear floor in lithium prices, there's no strong reason to add. Hold what you have but watch closely.

watch_today.title: VTS.AX — Brace for catch-up selling tonight
watch_today.detail: VTS.AX closed up 0.31% today, but the NASDAQ dropped 4.18% and the S&P 500 fell 2.64% last night. The ASX-listed ETF hasn't fully priced that in yet. When US markets open tonight (~11:30 PM AEST), expect more volatility. Nothing to act on now, but don't be surprised if VTS gives back gains in coming days.

watch_today.title: GXAI.AX — Down but analysts still bullish
watch_today.detail: GXAI fell 1.74% today tracking the NASDAQ lower, and is now 5.15% below your cost base. But multiple analysts this week (Motley Fool, Kalkine Media) named it as one of their top two ASX ETFs for the AI decade. The short-term pain is real, but the long-term thesis hasn't changed. Hold and consider adding on further weakness if you believe in the AI story.

watch_today.title: MSFT — Worst mover last night, watch AI regulation
watch_today.detail: Microsoft dropped 2.66% last night — the biggest single-night fall of your US holdings. Trump's new AI executive order could force companies like Microsoft to seek government approval before launching major AI models, which is a headwind for their Copilot and Azure AI ambitions. No reason to sell yet, but this regulatory story is developing and worth watching.

watch_today.title: FUEL.AX — Goldman cuts oil demand outlook
watch_today.detail: Goldman Sachs flagged a 'big hit' to global oil demand and cut their price forecasts. Crude oil fell to $90.54 last night. FUEL.AX is your energy ETF — if Goldman is right, this could be a sustained headwind. You're still slightly up on cost ($205.73 vs $200 invested), so no panic, but keep an eye on oil prices this week.

watch_today.title: AUD/USD dropped 1.16% last night — impacts your US holdings
watch_today.detail: The Aussie dollar fell from 71.3c to 70.5c US last night. A weaker AUD actually helps your US holdings (GOOG, MSFT, TTWO) when converted back to AUD — so the AUD fall partially cushions the US share price drops. Worth keeping in mind when you see the numbers.

markets.summary: Last night was ugly on Wall Street — the NASDAQ shed 4.18% and the S&P 500 dropped 2.64%, the kind of broad selloff that hits everything. The ASX followed with a more modest -0.70% decline today. Oil fell 2.69% to $90.54 a barrel after Goldman Sachs cut their demand outlook, and gold dropped 2.47% to $4,365. The Aussie dollar also slipped 1.16% to 70.5 US cents.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Modest decline today, following Wall Street's lead but cushioned by local factors.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Sharp selloff last night — broad market risk-off move, worst session in weeks.

indicators.name: NASDAQ Composite
indicators.note: Heavy tech selloff last night, likely linked to Trump's AI regulation order spooking growth stocks.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Goldman Sachs cut their global oil demand forecast, sending crude lower last night.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Gold fell sharply last night in a broad commodity pullback — unusual as gold usually holds up in selloffs.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: Aussie dollar weakened last night — partially cushions US holding losses when converted to AUD.

politics.summary: No Australian political stories were available in today's data feed. The politics section is quiet on the domestic front today.

ai.summary: The big AI story this weekend is US government intervention — Trump signed an executive order that could require AI companies to get federal approval before launching major models. Separately, the CEOs of OpenAI, Google, Anthropic and Microsoft jointly lobbied Congress on biosecurity. And China is aggressively poaching top AI talent from US labs.

stories.title: Trump's AI order could force OpenAI, Google and Anthropic to seek approval before launching models
stories.why_it_matters: Trump's new executive order signals a major shift in how the US government wants to oversee AI. Rather than letting companies like OpenAI, Google and Anthropic self-regulate, the order could require federal sign-off before major new models are released to the public. This adds a layer of compliance cost and potential delays for AI products — a headwind for companies like Alphabet (GOOG) and Microsoft (MSFT) whose growth stories are increasingly AI-driven. It also puts the White House and OpenAI on a collision course, as the two reportedly have competing visions for what AI rules should look like.

stories.title: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and Microsoft CEOs ask Congress to mandate synthetic DNA screening
stories.why_it_matters: In a rare show of unity, the CEOs of OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and Microsoft jointly wrote to the US Congress asking for a law requiring DNA synthesis companies to screen orders for dangerous pathogens — basically, stopping bad actors from using AI to design bioweapons. It's a sign the industry is getting ahead of biosecurity concerns before regulators force their hand, and shows these competitors are willing to cooperate when the stakes are high enough.

stories.title: Tencent hires former OpenAI researcher Yao Shunyu as Chief AI Scientist in AGI push
stories.why_it_matters: China's Tencent has poached top OpenAI researcher Yao Shunyu as its new Chief AI Scientist, part of a broader push toward AGI (Artificial General Intelligence — AI that can think and reason like a human across any task). This is the latest in a string of high-profile talent moves from US labs to Chinese tech giants, intensifying the US-China AI race. For investors in US AI stocks, it's a reminder that the competitive moat is narrowing.

stories.title: Is AI too important to leave to private investors? Trump thinks so
stories.why_it_matters: The Trump administration is signalling it sees AI as a national strategic asset — too important to leave entirely in the hands of private companies and investors. This framing could lead to more government involvement in AI development, potentially including public funding, strategic direction, or export controls. It's a significant shift from the previous hands-off approach and could reshape how companies like OpenAI and Google operate in the US.

sport.summary: Wild weekend in the NRL — Panthers demolished the Tigers 68-0 in the most lopsided result of the season, while the Titans pulled off an upset at Suncorp to put the Broncos' season in serious trouble. The Dolphins also ran over the Cowboys 40-14. In AFL, Fremantle hammered North Melbourne in what's being called a record thrashing. Nick Kyrgios confirmed another tennis comeback ahead of Wimbledon.

stories.title: Panthers thrash Wests Tigers 68-0 — Nathan Cleary fires State of Origin warning
stories.why_it_matters: Penrith ran riot at CommBank Stadium today, beating Wests Tigers 68-0 — the biggest scoreline of the NRL season. The Tigers were booed off by their own fans. Nathan Cleary was in sublime form, reportedly using the performance as a direct message ahead of State of Origin. It raises Blues selection headaches with Origin approaching. The Tigers are in a genuine crisis — fans and the club are asking hard questions about the roster and coaching staff.

stories.title: Titans stun Broncos 28-23 at Suncorp — Brisbane's season in deep trouble
stories.why_it_matters: The Gold Coast Titans pulled off a stunning 28-23 upset over the Brisbane Broncos at Suncorp Stadium last night. A young Titans gun conjured the match-winning moment in what Fox Sports described as a 'Suncorp miracle.' The Broncos' season is now in genuine crisis — coach Michael Maguire (Madge) is under fire and Brisbane's top-eight prospects are fading. Gold Coast fans will be buzzing.

stories.title: Dolphins run over Cowboys 40-14 — fifth straight win as Origin stars shine
stories.why_it_matters: The Dolphins beat the North Queensland Cowboys 40-14 yesterday, their fifth win in a row. Origin stars were in top form for the Phins. A Cowboys player also learned their fate for a third high-tackle offence this season — expect a suspension. The Dolphins are quietly building into finals contenders.

stories.title: Fremantle belt North Melbourne in record AFL thrashing — Clarkson 'bitterly disappointed'
stories.why_it_matters: Fremantle hammered North Melbourne in what ESPN and AFL.com.au are calling a record thrashing on Saturday. North Melbourne coach Chris 'Clarko' Clarkson called his team 'bitterly disappointed' in what was described as the biggest loss of his celebrated coaching career. Fremantle are putting pressure on the top four and raising serious questions about whether Clarkson can turn North around.

stories.title: Nick Kyrgios confirms tennis comeback — Wimbledon charge on
stories.why_it_matters: Nick Kyrgios has confirmed yet another return to professional tennis, with Wimbledon in his sights. The latest comeback is confirmed and Kyrgios is reportedly targeting the grass court season. Given his record at Wimbledon (finalist in 2022), he's always a chance on grass if his body holds up. Australian tennis fans will be watching closely.
